title: task: implement ContainerManager with real Bollard Docker API calls
description:
Replace the three stub methods in src/runner/container.rs with real Bollard API calls.

create_container(name):
- Pull image if not present (respect pull_policy from config: always/if-not-present/never)
- Create container with: image from config (default ubuntu:22.04), memory_limit, cpu_quota,
  network access, /tmp mounted as tmpfs for installer scratch space
- Set environment: DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive, HOME=/root, PATH includes /usr/local/bin,
  CI=true, NONINTERACTIVE=1 (non-interactive flags bead adds to this list)
- Container naming convention: afsc-INSTALLERNAME-TIMESTAMP (e.g. afsc-rust-20260406-143022)
  for easy identification in docker ps during debugging
- Return the real container ID string from Bollard

exec_in_container(container_id, command):
- Use bollard::exec to create and start an exec instance inside the running container
- Stream stdout and stderr separately into String buffers
- Return (exit_code, stdout, stderr) tuple
- Handle timeout via tokio::time::timeout wrapping the exec stream
- On timeout, kill the exec and return a timeout-specific error

cleanup_container(container_id):
- Stop the container (with 10s grace period)
- Remove the container (force=true to handle edge cases)
- Log any cleanup failures but do not propagate them (best-effort)
- CRITICAL: cleanup must run even on Ctrl-C / SIGINT / task cancellation.
  Use Drop trait or tokio::select! with a cancellation token to ensure containers
  are not leaked on abort. Leaked containers waste disk and memory.

Must import bollard::{Docker, container::*, exec::*} and connect to the local Docker socket.
The Docker client should be created once in ContainerManager::new() and reused.
Reference: bollard 0.16 API - use Docker::connect_with_local_defaults().
close_reason: Implemented ContainerManager with real Bollard 0.16 API: create_container (pull policy, env vars, tmpfs, naming convention), exec_in_container (streamed stdout/stderr, exit code inspection), cleanup_container (stop + force remove, best-effort). Added ContainerGuard with Drop-based cleanup for leak prevention. Added PullPolicy enum.

title: task: refactor executor.rs to run installers inside Docker containers instead of locally
description:

1. Create a fresh Docker container via ContainerManager
2. Execute the curl|bash command INSIDE the container via exec_in_container
3. Capture stdout/stderr/exit_code from the container exec
4. Classify the result using the existing error classifier
5. Cleanup the container via cleanup_container (always, even on failure)

The execution flow becomes:
  create_container -> exec_in_container(curl -fsSL URL | bash -s -- FLAGS) -> classify -> cleanup

Keep the existing retry logic - retries should create a NEW container each attempt.
Keep the existing timeout logic - but apply it to the container exec, not a local process.

SCOPE: This bead is ONLY about the Docker execution path. The existing local execution
code should NOT be deleted - it will be refactored into a --local fallback in a separate
bead (74o.14). Introduce an ExecutionBackend trait or enum with Docker and Local variants
so the executor can dispatch to either mode.

Key: the executor must pass the installer URL from the checksums entry, not construct it.
The curl|bash pattern is: curl -fsSL 'URL' | bash -s -- [FLAGS]
close_reason: Refactored executor.rs with ExecutionBackend enum (Docker/Local). Docker path: create container → exec curl|bash inside → capture output → cleanup with guard. title: task: implement SHA256 checksum verification before installer execution
description:
CRITICAL SECURITY GAP: The tool has InstallerTest.expected_sha256, TestResult.checksum_result,
and a full ChecksumResult struct (matches, expected, actual, url, download_ms, size_bytes) but
the executor NEVER ACTUALLY VERIFIES CHECKSUMS. It pipes curl|bash directly, with no opportunity
to verify the hash before execution.

This is the tools CORE security value proposition. ACFS checksums.yaml contains SHA256 hashes
for all 41 installer scripts. The tool MUST verify them.

CURRENT (broken):
  curl -fsSL URL | bash -s --
  (script is piped directly to bash, checksum never checked)

CORRECT:
  1. Download to temp file: curl -fsSL URL -o /tmp/installer_NAME.sh
  2. Compute SHA256 of downloaded file
  3. Compare against test.expected_sha256 from checksums.yaml
  4. If match (or no expected hash provided): execute bash /tmp/installer_NAME.sh
  5. If MISMATCH: FAIL immediately with checksum_mismatch error classification, do NOT execute
  6. Populate result.checksum_result with: matches, expected, actual, download_ms, size_bytes

Implementation in both Docker and local modes:
- Docker mode: download inside the container to a temp path, sha256sum, compare, then execute
- Local mode: download to temp dir, sha256sum, compare, then execute

The ChecksumResult struct already exists at runner/installer.rs:30 and test.with_checksum_result()
already exists at line 128. The wiring just needs to be added to the executor.

This must be done AFTER the executor refactor (74o.1.2) since the execution flow changes.

Security implication: without this, a compromised upstream URL would silently execute malicious
code. This verification is the entire reason ACFS maintains checksums.yaml.
close_reason: Implemented SHA256 checksum verification in both Docker and Local modes. Docker: shell script downloads to temp file, sha256sum, compare, execute or fail with exit 99. Local: Rust-native sha2 crate verification before execution. Checksum mismatch prevents script execution. Added tests for verified script generation.

title: task: add non-interactive flags and environment for installer execution
description:

execution in BOTH Docker and local modes.

- DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive (apt-get wont prompt)
- RUSTUP_INIT_SKIP_PATH_CHECK=yes
- NONINTERACTIVE=1 (generic flag some scripts check)
- CI=true (many scripts detect CI and skip prompts)

FOR DOCKER MODE: set these in the container environment via Bollard Env config
when creating the container in ContainerManager.

FOR LOCAL MODE: export these before spawning the bash subprocess in the local executor.

The key insight: ACFS own installer scripts are designed to run non-interactively
when invoked by the main install.sh. We just need to set the same env vars that
install.sh sets. DO NOT blindly append -y to all installer invocations - not all
scripts accept it. The env vars are the universal approach.

Evidence: rustup failed with Unable to run interactively. Run with -y because the
container had no TTY and no -y flag. Setting CI=true would have fixed this.

title: task: implement worker pool for parallel installer testing
description:
Replace the semaphore skeleton in runner/parallel.rs with a real worker pool.

Implementation using tokio mpsc channel pattern:
1. Create a channel: tx/rx for InstallerTest items
2. Spawn N worker tasks (N = --parallel flag, default 1)
3. Each worker loops: receive test from channel, call the executor (which dispatches
   to Docker or local mode based on config), send result back via results channel
4. Main task: send all tests to tx, then collect results from results rx
5. Progress reporting: print status line as each test completes (name, pass/fail, duration)

IMPORTANT: The worker pool calls the EXECUTOR abstraction, not Docker directly. This
means parallel execution works in both Docker mode and --local mode. Each worker gets
its own execution context (its own container in Docker mode, its own temp dir in local).

Fail-fast mode (--fail-fast):
- When a test fails, signal all workers to stop accepting new work
- Workers finish their current test but do not pick up new ones
- Use a shared AtomicBool or tokio CancellationToken

Concurrency safety:
- Each worker gets its own execution context (no shared state)
- Results channel handles ordering
- Progress output needs a mutex or single-writer pattern to avoid interleaved lines

title: epic: close every README gap found in the 2026-09-01 reality check
description:
## Why this epic exists
A full reality check on 2026-09-01 (read every source file, ran every CLI command, real Docker runs, a fake
`claude` shim, a local webhook receiver, a SIGTERM-mid-run test) found that the core loop works (download,
SHA-256 verify, run in a fresh non-root Docker container, retry, persist, serve metrics) but that roughly half
of the README's promises are stale, unwired, unsafe, or broken as shipped. Zero open beads existed; the bead
graph said 100% done while the product delivered about 55% of its README.

## Headline findings (each is a child epic below)
- Classification never attached to results; JSON/JSONL stdout corrupted by log lines; retry history lost;
  results files collide on same-second runs; SIGTERM leaks containers.
- Eight documented config keys are dead; partial config sections fail to parse; shipped default image differs
  from the code default and runs installers as root (false failures, 26 s overhead per installer).
- Execution does not mirror ACFS (interpreter, args, env, file-vs-stdin); no full-catalog run ever done.
- `--remediate` runs `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` in the ACFS repo, applies no safety check, and
  reports success unconditionally.
- Shipped systemd units pass flags clap rejects; the notify script parses nonexistent keys.
- 16 of 18 bash E2E scripts never invoke the binary; Docker tests are ignored and non-blocking; CI smoke is
  hidden by `|| true`; CI has been red since May on 8 RustSec advisories.
- README counts, default image, categories, examples, and remediation claims are wrong; CHANGELOG stale.

## Live value already demonstrated
`validate --check-hashes` found 7 of 48 ACFS installer checksums drifted (atuin, bv, caam, casr, grok,
rust, uv). Nothing runs that on a schedule. The nightly canary child epic fixes that.

## Architecture spine every child must respect
1. One resolved `Settings` object (defaults < file < `AFSC_*` env < explicitly passed CLI flags).
2. One `InstallerSpec` (checksums entry + built-in ACFS profile + `[installers.<name>]` overrides).
3. One executor contract: failures always carry classification, checksum tri-state, full attempt history,
   bounded captures.
4. One container lifecycle owner: fallible construction, labels, cancellation token, orphan reaper,
   hash-tagged images.
5. One `RunReport`, many sinks (human, JSON, JSONL, persister, metrics, notifier, structured log).
6. Stdout is data, stderr is logs, exit codes are policy (0 ok, 1 installer failures, 2 usage/config,
   3 infrastructure, 130/143 interrupted). Never `std::process::exit` from a handler.
7. Remediation is a mode with a policy (off | advisory | propose | apply); checksum drift is fixed
   deterministically without an LLM.
8. Proof at four layers: unit, CLI integration (no Docker), Docker integration (blocking), nightly canary.
9. Docs derive from truth (drift tests).

## Waves (see child epics; `br ready` will surface the order)
Wave 0 CI green; Wave 1 core loop; Wave 2 config and fidelity; Wave 3 proof; Wave 4 reporting and
deployment; Wave 5 remediation; Wave 6 canary, docs, release, final integration.

title: task: attach ErrorClassification to every failed TestResult in both backends
description:
## Context (vision goal 3, 8, 15)
README promises automatic error classification of failures. The classifier (`src/parser/classifier.rs`) works
and the `classify-error` command works, but the executor never stores a classification on the result.
Evidence: `src/runner/executor.rs` `run_test_docker` (lines ~215-402) and `run_test_local` (~405-622) set
`status`, `success`, `exit_code`, `stderr` on failure but never `result.error`. `classify_error` is only
called inside `should_retry_result` (~665-681) to decide retries. Consequences observed on 2026-09-01:
`status --format json` shows `"error_classification": null` for a dependency failure ("E: Unable to locate
package foo", exit 100), a checksum mismatch, and a connection-refused download; the Slack payload listed
`dep_fail_tool (unknown)`.

Also: the srps installer's refusal ("Don't run this script as root") is printed on stdout, which the
classifier never sees, so classification must consider a stdout tail too.

## Target state
Every result whose status is Failed, TimedOut, or Cancelled carries `Some(ErrorClassification)`.
Classification input = stderr + last 4 KB of stdout, plus a synthetic marker for cases where the failure is
known structurally: checksum mismatch (`CHECKSUM_MISMATCH: …`), timeout (`Test timed out after Ns`),
download failure, container execution error, cancellation.

## Implementation
1. `src/runner/executor.rs`: add `fn finalize_failure(result: &mut TestResult, synthetic: Option<&str>)`.
   It builds the text as `synthetic.unwrap_or("")` + "
" + stderr + "
" + stdout tail (4 KB), calls
   `classify_error(&text, result.exit_code.unwrap_or(-1))`, and sets `result.error` when it is `None`.
   Call it at every failure return in both backends: checksum mismatch, non-zero exit, exec error, timeout,
   download failure, and in `src/runner/parallel.rs` (~63-66) for the "Execution error" path.
2. `src/parser/classifier.rs`: add `is_timeout` (pattern `(?i)test timed out after`) → category `timeout`,
   severity `Transient`, retryable `false` (timeouts are not retried by policy; see C3), suggestion
   "increase timeout or add an [installers.<name>] override"; add root-refusal patterns
   `(?i)don't run (this|the) script as root`, `(?i)must not be run as root`, `(?i)refus\w+ to run as root`
   → category `permission` with suggestion "run as a non-root user (the default afsc-base image does)";
   add `cancelled` category for token cancellation (non-retryable).
3. `src/main.rs` human printer: under each failed installer print
   `error: <category> (<severity>, retryable=<bool>, confidence=<n>%)` and the suggestion line.
   `status --detailed` already prints when `Some`; verify it does after this change.
4. Add fixtures `tests/unit/fixtures/error_outputs/root_refused.txt` and `timeout.txt`.

## Files
- src/runner/executor.rs, src/runner/parallel.rs, src/parser/classifier.rs, src/main.rs,
  tests/unit/fixtures/error_outputs/*.txt

## Success criteria
- [ ] Unit: every failure exit path in both backends yields `error.is_some()` (local backend tested with
      file:// fixtures; Docker path covered by C9).
- [ ] Unit: classifier maps the root-refusal fixtures to `permission`, the timeout marker to `timeout`.
- [ ] Human output shows the error line and suggestion for a failing fixture.
- [ ] No behavior change for passing installers (`error` stays `None`).

## Dependencies
None. C4 (persistence) and M5 (notifications) consume this.

## Considerations
Keep `classify_error` pure and cheap; it compiles regexes on every call today (see m4 for a `OnceLock`
regex cache, optional). Do not change retry decisions here; C3 owns retry policy.

title: task: cancellation token, signal handling, container labels, orphan reaper, fallible ContainerManager
description:
## Context (vision goal 21, 11)
`cmd_check` has no signal handling. `ContainerGuard::drop` (`src/runner/container.rs:528-549`) spawns a
thread with a new runtime, which never runs when the process is killed. Observed 2026-09-01: `timeout -s TERM
8 … check mdwb` left `afsc-mdwb-20260901-235647-951-a53a` running with the installer still executing inside.
`systemctl stop` sends SIGTERM, so the systemd story leaks a container per stop. `ContainerManager::new`
panics via `expect` (`container.rs:70-73`). Containers carry no labels, so orphans cannot be identified
safely.

## Target state
- A `CancellationToken` (tokio_util) is created in `cmd_check`, cancelled by SIGINT/SIGTERM, and threaded
  through `ParallelRunner`, `InstallerTestRunner`, and `ContainerManager::exec_in_container`.
- On cancel: each worker stops and removes its container (5 s grace), records status `Cancelled` with a
  classification (`cancelled`), the run persists with `interrupted: true`, watchdog STOPPING is sent, and
  the process exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) by returning an `Interrupted` error to `main`.
- Every container gets labels `afsc.managed=true`, `afsc.run_id`, `afsc.installer`, `afsc.created_at`
  (RFC3339), `afsc.pid`, `afsc.version`.
- Startup reaper (config `docker.reap_orphans`, default true): list containers with `afsc.managed=true`,
  remove those whose `afsc.pid` is not alive or whose age exceeds `2 × timeout`; log each removal at WARN.
  Never touch containers without the label. `check --reap` runs only the reaper and exits.
- `ContainerManager::try_new() -> Result<Self>`; the old `new` is removed.

## Implementation
1. Cargo.toml: add `tokio-util = { version = "0.7", features = ["rt"] }`.
2. `src/runner/container.rs`: labels in `create_container`; `reap_orphans(&self, max_age)`; `try_new`;
   `exec_in_container` takes `&CancellationToken` and uses `tokio::select!`; on cancel, stop + remove.
3. `src/runner/executor.rs` and `parallel.rs`: accept the token; `Cancelled` status; skip queued tests when
   cancelled.
4. `src/main.rs`: install handler with `tokio::signal::ctrl_c` and `unix::signal(SIGTERM)`; after cancel,
   wait for workers (bounded 15 s); persist partial run; map to exit code.
5. New `TestStatus::Cancelled`; update `status` icons and summary counts.

## Files
- Cargo.toml, src/runner/container.rs, src/runner/executor.rs, src/runner/parallel.rs,
  src/runner/installer.rs, src/main.rs

## Success criteria
- [ ] Docker: SIGTERM 5 s into a slow fixture → zero `afsc.managed` containers within 10 s; results file has
      `interrupted: true`; exit code 143.
- [ ] Docker: a labeled container with a dead pid is reaped; an unlabeled `sleep` container is untouched.
- [ ] Unit: bad `DOCKER_HOST` → `Err`, no panic.

## Dependencies
None. M4 (exit codes) and M11 (fail-fast cancel) reuse the token.

## Considerations
`ContainerGuard` stays as best effort. The reaper must be conservative: label match AND (dead pid OR too
old). Document `check --reap` in README.

title: task: deterministic checksum-drift remediation — candidate checksums.yaml, Docker verification, optional branch and PR
description:
## Context (vision goal 6, 13)
Checksum drift is the most common failure class and needs no LLM: download, hash, regenerate the entry,
verify the installer still runs with the new hash, hand a reviewable diff to a human. ACFS's own generator is
`./scripts/lib/security.sh --update-checksums` and its recovery flow lives in `handle_checksum_mismatch`.

## Target state
- Library `src/remediation/checksums.rs`: `plan_refresh(results | hash_checks) -> RefreshPlan { entries:
  [{name, url, old, new, script_diff_summary}] }`; `render_candidate(checksums, plan) -> String` in the
  ACFS format (M9 shares the renderer); `verify_entry(spec_with_new_hash)` runs the installer through the
  Docker executor (fresh container) and records pass/fail.
- Subcommand `remediate checksums [--from-last-run | --check-hashes] [--advisory|--propose|--apply]
  [--only <names>]`: advisory prints the unified diff and per-entry verification results; propose creates a
  git worktree of the ACFS repo on branch `afsc/checksum-refresh-<date>`, writes the candidate, commits with
  a message listing installers and old/new hashes, and runs `gh pr create --fill` when
  `remediation.create_pr`; apply additionally pushes (never to main). Entries whose verification failed are
  excluded and reported.
- Script diff summary: store the last verified script bytes per installer under `<data_dir>/scripts/<name>/
  <sha256>` so drift reports can show `diff` size and a unified diff preview (helps a reviewer judge
  legitimacy).
- Wired into `check --remediate`: for results with `checksum_mismatch`, run this path first.

## Success criteria
- [ ] CLI (C8d): drift fixture → advisory prints the diff and verification; propose creates the branch in a
      temp git repo with the new hash and a well-formed commit message; excluded entries reported.
- [ ] Candidate matches the ACFS format golden sample.

title: task: add [notifications], [monitoring], [watchdog] config sections to schema.rs
description:
README documents three config sections that don't exist in src/config/schema.rs. This bead adds them WITH proper mapping to existing internal types.

CRITICAL DESIGN DECISION — Config shape vs internal types:
The README shows a flat config:
  [notifications]
  enabled = false
  slack_webhook = ""
  github_issue_repo = ""
  email = ""

But the existing notify.rs code has nested types:
  NotificationConfig { github: Option<GitHubConfig>, slack: Option<SlackConfig> }
  GitHubConfig { repo, token_env, create_issues, add_comments }
  SlackConfig { webhook_url_env, channel, notify_on_failure, notify_on_success }

RESOLUTION: The config TOML struct should be user-friendly (flat, matching README).
A conversion method maps it to the internal NotificationConfig for the Notifier.

SECURITY: Secrets (GitHub token, Slack webhook URL) should NOT be stored in config TOML.
Config stores the ENV VAR NAMES that hold the secrets, not the secrets themselves.
  slack_webhook_env = "SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"  (env var name, not the URL)
  github_token_env = "GITHUB_TOKEN"        (env var name, not the token)
  github_issue_repo = "owner/repo"         (not a secret, can be in config)

EMAIL: README lists email = "" but no email implementation exists or is planned.
Remove email from the config schema and update README to drop it. Email notifications
are out of scope for a CLI tool — Slack and GitHub cover the notification use cases.

Implementation in src/config/schema.rs:

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct NotificationsConfig {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub enabled: bool,                          // default false
    #[serde(default)]
    pub slack_webhook_env: String,              // env var holding webhook URL
    #[serde(default)]
    pub slack_channel: String,                  // default empty (uses webhook default)
    #[serde(default)]
    pub github_token_env: String,               // env var holding GH token
    #[serde(default)]
    pub github_issue_repo: String,              // 'owner/repo' format
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub notify_on_failure: bool,                // default true
    #[serde(default)]
    pub notify_on_success: bool,                // default false
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct MonitoringConfig {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub health_endpoint: bool,                  // default false
    #[serde(default = "default_health_port")]
    pub health_port: u16,                       // default 8080
    #[serde(default)]
    pub metrics_enabled: bool,                  // default false
    #[serde(default = "default_metrics_port")]
    pub metrics_port: u16,                      // default 9090
}
